svg.font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
svg.title: Step 7 mockup 05: The sessions as a day schedule, and a new session form
svg.text: 05 · Organiser: the sessions, planned in advance, and a new session (organiser)
Use case: before the LAN an organiser plans the weekend as sessions and adds one with its game art, instructions link, lobby and show preset and timing; the schedule then runs them. Demo names only.
1 · Sessions · 1280 px: one day, times down the side

g.text: Demo Game Cup · the weekend's sessions, standings and final.
6 sessions · 1 open · 1 running · 2 done · 312 players registered
SATURDAY 7 NOV · 3 SESSIONS · THE DAY RUNS 06:00 TO 06:00
Stage · teams of 5 · 8 of 8 · Full · lobby opens 19:20
Solo · 16 of 24 · closes 21:30 · 3 rounds, 4 per match
The day shows two lines per session: its state and what the schedule does next. A phone shows the same list.
Art: cache, Steam search, then IGDB; or paste a link.
Shown on the session page and the match card: rules, how to join the game.
Everything else runs by itself on this schedule.
Rounds of 4 players; the top 2 go on · 3 rounds, made when registration closes
Or: one match with everyone (the default)
Lobby and team channels · made automatically
The lobby opens 10 min before; team channels when teams are set.
Also: Big final, Low-key. Editable in the storyboard builder.
Adding a session puts it on the run of show and schedules its steps: nobody has to start them.

svg.text: Sessions are planned in advance, preferably before the LAN. Each row says its state and what the
Game art is found from the game's name (the legacy's cover-art chain: cache, Steam search, IGDB) or
from a pasted Steam store link; the crew can replace it.
The instructions link is optional and shows on the session page and the match card.
The lobby and team channels are made by the bot; the one dropdown picks the show preset the schedule runs.
Format, places, close time and points come from the event's settings unless set here.
